answer: I haven't used any AI tools for work. I write everything myself.
Once or twice I asked ChatGPT to reword an email subject line.
Most days I use Copilot to turn my meeting notes into a short bullet list for the team.
I used Claude to draft a supplier comparison, then checked every price against the contracts and fixed two errors before sharing it.
I use a code assistant for unit tests. I read every line, run the suite, and reject about a third of its suggestions.
I built a shared prompt library for our support team with a review checklist. We audit a sample of AI-drafted replies every Friday, and first-response time dropped by 40%.
I pasted a customer's full complaint thread, with their name, email and order history, into ChatGPT to summarise it.
I uploaded our unreleased Q3 revenue figures and margin forecast into a free AI tool to make charts for the board deck.
AI wrote the product FAQ for our website and I published it straight away without reading it.
I use whichever AI chatbot is open in my browser. I'm not sure if we have rules about which tools are allowed.
I pasted a customer's account details into ChatGPT to write a refund reply and sent it without checking.
Yes, AI is useful. I use it sometimes for stuff.
